plan:
WHAT IT WILL TRADE: It picks a side from the day's structure and only adds to that side on a pullback after a new high/low (never on a turn call), and it refuses to ever take a trade against its declared side.

HOW IT TRIES TO BEAT THE CHAMPION: This is NOT a change to how it enters or picks sides — rules 1-6 and 8-10 are byte-identical to the champion (iteration 2). The only change is a patch to one claim-exception sentence in rule 7, closing a loophole where it was buying straight back into the same stall it had just banked profit from, so this run is partly a repeat of the champion and partly a narrow mechanism check on whether that one patch holds, not a swing for a bigger number.

WHAT WOULD HAVE TO HAPPEN: On the tape, after it banks a profit on a leg, it has to actually sit out that direction until price makes a brand-new high or low beyond where that trade peaked, instead of buying the same stall back within minutes.

WHAT IT GIVES UP: It will sit out one real continuation leg it would otherwise have caught right after a claim (the June $2,438 winner it would have blocked), trading a few good re-entries to avoid the much larger number of bad ones.

BIGGEST RISK: With only two day-runs first and the champion comparison running in pairs of two, any $/day difference this size will land inside the known $324/day noise floor, so the run can easily look flat or even slightly worse without that meaning the fix failed — the real verdict here is whether it stops buying back the stall, not the headline dollar number.

audit.raw:
VERDICT: GO
FAILING METRIC: $/day ($620/day best-of-three vs bar ≥800, a $180/day gap)
AIMED AT IT: PARTLY — the guard removes a named loss source (5 of 9 IT4 same-side re-entries cost −$1,002) but the pre-registered tests (P1–P5) score mechanism/counts, not $/day directly — correctly deferring the dollar verdict per L10.
MEASURABLE: YES — the cited mechanism effect (−$1,002 from the 5 re-entries the guard would block, out of 2 days) exceeds the $324/day noise floor, even though $/day itself stays unresolved until several tranches accumulate.
MISSING: (1) the tranche stop rule checks only cumulative net + P1/P3 — it should also carry worst-day and CV (the full dominance gate) per tranche, or a tail-worsening IT5 could survive several tranches before being caught; (2) no stated action if STEP 1 shows partial (not zero) obedience to the 60-min guard, only a clean pass/fail; (3) nothing else — trade citations, mechanical guard verification, and quarantine protocol are already in place.
REASON: This is a single well-evidenced rule edit (L2/L3/L0c all satisfied, named trades, mechanical guard check) targeting a real defect surfaced in IT4's own trades, not a re-derivation of settled ground. It should run, but widen the tranche-stop check to the full consistency gate before reading any tranche as progress.
